lines.text: Supply counter. Student card, please. Well, your face will do, I know everyone.
Hello, {player}! Run out of practice shuriken again?
Come in. Quick, before the bell. The queue's long after the throwing lesson.
Good morning. Notebooks, brushes, practice gear. What'll it be?
You've graduated! This counter is for students only now. Try the weapon shop on the market street.
Practice kunai, blunt-tipped. Practice shuriken, rubber-edged. Nobody loses an eye on my watch.
Notebooks ruled for hand signs, and brushes for the calligraphy lesson.
Training weights for your ankles. The taijutsu teacher recommends them, your legs won't.
Target paper by the sheet. Draw your own rings if you like.
{item}. {pay}. Don't lose it on the first day.
Here you go. Write your name on it.
That's {pay}. Study hard!
One {item}, student price. {pay}.
{pay}. Bring it back if it breaks in a lesson, I'll swap it.
Short? Your stipend comes in tomorrow. Come back then.
Not enough. Borrow from the lending box, under the counter. Return it clean.
A little under. The plain notebook is cheaper and has the same pages.
Out of {item}. Every first-year bought one this week.
No practice kunai left. The yard eats them, I swear.
The counter shuts when the last lesson ends. Hurry.
Closing! Go home and do your homework.
Buy a spare brush. They always split the week before the written test.
The {item}. Every teacher here used one as a student.
Ankle weights, if you want to be faster at the obstacle course. Take them off for the test.
Practice shuriken are cheap. Throw a hundred a day, and the real ones will feel easy.
You again! You go through more target paper than the whole class.
I saved you a good brush. The rest of the batch is scratchy.
Welcome! Grab a table with a grill, they're all hot.
Come in, come in! Smell that? That's the good stuff.
Hello, {player}! Table for one, or are friends on the way?
Welcome to the barbecue house. Eat until you can't, then eat a little more.
There's a free grill by the window. Sit, I'll bring the tongs.
Welcome to our house! In the Akimichi kitchen, nobody leaves hungry. Not once, not ever.
Pork belly, beef tongue, chicken thigh, and the vegetables nobody orders.
The platters are for squads. One plate of everything, three hungry Genin, one sweaty grill.
Marinated or salted? Salted for the first plate, marinated for the second, that's the rule.
Rice comes in bowls or buckets. I'm only half joking.
Grilled onigiri too, crusty with soy. Order them before the meat or they'll get forgotten.
A plate of {item}! Lay it flat, don't crowd the grill.
{pay}. Turn it once, only once.
Here's your plate. Tongs for the raw, chopsticks for the cooked. Don't mix them.
That's {pay}. Shout if the grill needs more coals.
Coming right up! Big appetite today, I see.
{item}, sliced thin. That's {pay}.
There you go! Wait for the sizzle before you flip.
Not quite enough for the platter. A single plate, then?
You're short. The grilled onigiri are cheaper and they're half the joy.
Hmm, that won't cover it. Come back with your squad and split it.
A few ryo under. Eat what you can afford, and come back richer.
Out of {item}! A table of Chunin just ate the whole cut.
No more tongue tonight. The butcher comes at dawn.
All gone. The last squad was very, very hungry.
Haggle? Eat more. That's the only discount in here: the third plate is cheaper.
No, but a squad that cleans its plates gets a free dessert.
I don't cut prices, I cut meat. Thick, thin, however you like it.
Help scrub the grills tonight and the next plate's on the house.
Last orders for the grill! After this the coals go out.
We're closing soon. One more plate for the road?
The kitchen's winding down. Order now or dream about pork belly.
Sparring tomorrow? Eat barbecue tonight. It puts a little more weight behind your punches for a while.
The {special}, today only. Cut this morning.
Pork belly first. Fat on the grill makes everything after it taste better.
The {item}. Don't argue, just try it.
Before a taijutsu lesson, a plate of beef. Your fists will feel it.
Come with your whole squad. Barbecue tastes better split four ways.
You again! Your usual table's free. I wiped it twice.
I'm starting to think you live on barbecue. Good. I approve.
A regular! There's an extra plate of vegetables for you. You're welcome, and eat them.
Your grill's already heating. I saw you coming down the street.
Your table's ready! The grill's lit and the first plate's on its way.
{item}, coming through! Hot plate, mind your sleeves.
Reservation for your squad? Back corner, the big grill. All set.
Your platter's up. Lay it on slowly, let the fat talk.
Coming with a squad? Book a table a day ahead. On a busy night there's not a free grill in the house.
Welcome! Shoes in the cubbies, please, then through the curtain.
Come in. The water's hot, the steam's thick and the floor is slippery.
Good evening, {player}. A soak after a long day?
Hello there. Towels on the left, soap on the right, worries outside.
Welcome to the bath. Wash first, soak second. The rule's on the wall.
Cold out there! Come in, the big pool's been steaming since noon.
Soaked already? Then you're halfway to a bath. Come in and finish the job.
Entry covers the hot pool, the cold pool and the steam room.
Towels are extra. Bring your own and save a ryo.
Fruit milk in the cooler. It's a crime to leave the bath without one.
Soap, scrub cloths and a little bottle of camellia oil for sore shoulders.
The outdoor pool looks up at the Hokage Rock. Best view in the Leaf, if you ask me.
In you go. {pay}. Leave the door ajar if the steam gets too much.
That's {pay}. Your towel, folded.
Here's your {item}. Drink it standing up, hand on your hip. That's tradition.
{pay}, thank you. Soak until your fingers wrinkle.
A fresh towel and a locker key. Enjoy the water.
That's {pay}. The hot pool's quiet right now, perfect timing.
Short a ryo or two? Come back when you're flush, the water won't cool.
That's not enough for entry, I'm sorry. The river's free, if a bit cold.
Hmm, a little under. Skip the towel and it might just fit.
Not today. But the cooler's cheaper, if you want a fruit milk.
No more fruit milk, I'm afraid. A squad of Chunin drank the lot.
We're out of clean towels till the laundry's back. Bring your own today.
The {item}'s run out. Tomorrow, I promise.
Haggle for hot water? The fire under the boiler doesn't haggle with me.
Come at opening and it's a little cheaper. The water's the cleanest too.
Bring a friend and the second entry is half. Bathing's better with company.
No discounts, but nobody's ever thrown out for staying too long.
We drain the pools soon. Last soak of the night.
Closing in a little while. Don't fall asleep in the water.
I'm banking the boiler. You can have the pool to yourself till then.
After training all day, a long soak in the hot pool. Your muscles will forgive you by morning.
Hot pool, then cold, then hot again. My grandfather swore by it.
The {item}. It's the best thing in the cooler.
A bath before bed, then straight home to sleep. You'll wake feeling brand new.
The steam room, if you've got a cold coming. Breathe deep.
Your locker's free, number seven. I keep it for you.
A regular! I put a fruit milk in the cooler with your name on it.
You always come at the same hour. I've started setting the kettle by you.
Here again? You'll be the cleanest shinobi in the Leaf.
Welcome. Novels on the left, maps on the right, card packs at the counter.
Come in, {player}. Browse as long as you like, reading the first page is free.
Hello! Mind the stack by the door, it's the new arrivals and it's leaning.
Good day. If you're looking for something, I've probably read it.
Card packs? Top of the counter. The new set came in yesterday.
Adventure novels, ghost stories, histories of the Land of Fire. Something for every mood.
Maps of the village, the roads and the border country. The road maps are the best sellers.
Card packs: shinobi of legend, five to a pack. Collect the set, trade the doubles.
Cookbooks, poetry, books on herbs and birds. The quiet shelf, I call it.
The children's corner has picture books and a cushion. Grown-ups use it too.
{item}. {pay}. Don't fold the corners, use a bookmark.
Here you go. I'll wrap it in paper so the rain doesn't get it.
That's {pay}. Come and tell me how it ends. Actually, don't, I know how it ends.
One card pack, {pay}. Good luck! I hope it's a rare one.
{pay}, thank you. A good book is the cheapest journey there is.
Short. The secondhand shelf has the same stories for half the price.
That one's dear, I know. Read the first chapter here and come back when you can.
Not enough for the map. Copy the part you need, I won't tell.
Sold out of {item}. The printer in the capital is slow.
No card packs left! The Academy let out an hour ago.
Haggle? Trade me a book you've finished and I'll take something off.
The secondhand shelf is the haggling shelf. New books are new prices.
Closing soon. Finish the chapter, then off you go.
I'm blowing out the lamps. The books need their dark too.
A road map before any mission outside the wall. Getting lost costs more than the map.
The {item}. I stayed up till dawn with it. Don't make my mistake, start it at noon.
For a rainy day, a ghost story. For a sad day, a cookbook. Trust me.
Buy a card pack and trade the doubles at the Academy. That's half the fun.
I put a book aside for you. Don't ask how I knew. I just knew.
You've read more of my shop than I have, nearly. Nearly.
Here's my best reader. Sit, there's tea in the back.
Welcome. Speak softly, please, the new arrivals are still nervous.
Come in, and close the door quick. They'll be out in a flash.
Hello, {player}. Here to meet someone?
Welcome to the shelter. Sit on the cushion and wait. The cats choose you, not the other way round.
In you come. Mind the tabby on the step, that's where it likes to sleep.
Rainy days, every cat in the place piles into one basket. Come see.
The ones on the high shelf are shy. The ones on your lap are not.
Cat food on the shelf: dried fish, rice mash, and a jelly they go mad for.
Baskets, blankets and little bells on ribbons. The bells are for you, so you know where they are.
That one's been here longest. Very gentle, a little grumpy before breakfast.
Toys in the box. Feathers on sticks, mostly. They like the stick better.
{item}. {pay}. Your cat will pretend not to care, but it will.
Here you go. A bowl near the window, they like to eat and watch.
That's {pay}. Thank you for looking after one of ours.
Done. Every ryo here goes to food and blankets.
{pay}. If your cat ignores it for a day, don't worry, that's normal.
Yours. Bring a picture next time, we love to see where they end up.
Not quite enough. The dried fish is cheaper, and they love it more anyway.
You're a little short. Come and help clean the litter trays, we'll make it up.
That's beyond your purse today. The cats will still be here.
A few ryo shy. I can't lower it, the shelter barely covers its fish bills.
The {item}'s all gone. Donations come on Market Day.
No kittens just now, they all found homes this week. Isn't that lovely?
Out of stock. The fishmonger sends scraps tomorrow.
Haggling at a shelter? Bold. But every ryo here feeds a cat, so no.
If you give one of them a home, the food for the first week is free.
I can't do less. I can do an extra feather toy, though.
Volunteer a morning, and we'll talk about a discount.
Closing soon. Night is when they all wake up and want attention.
Last chance tonight. I'm doing the evening feed shortly.
We shut at dusk. Say goodbye to whoever's on your lap.
A cat suits a busy life. It'll keep the apartment warm while you're on missions.
The {item}. It's the one that makes the old tabby purr.
If you adopt, sit with your cat every day. That's how the trust grows.
A basket by the window. Cats like to watch the street almost as much as sleep.
Cats are tougher than they look. If yours gets into trouble, it'll get knocked out, not worse. Bring it straight here.
The grey one runs to the door when you come. Did you notice?
Back again! You're our best volunteer, even when you're not volunteering.
I saved the softest blanket for your cat. Take it home.
How's your cat? I think about every one of them after they leave.
Dango, fresh off the coals! Step right up.
Welcome! Three to a skewer, and every one of them round.
Hello, {player}! Sweet tooth acting up again?
Come and have a look, the syrup's still warm.
Hey there! The bench in the shade is free, if you want to sit.
Blossom season! The pink-white-green skewers are back, and they're selling like mad.
Afternoon snack time! The busiest hour of my whole day.
Soy glaze, sweet bean, or the three-colour ones. Those are the classics.
Sesame dango are new. A little nutty, a little salty.
The grilled ones have a char on them. Some people pick the char off. Those people are wrong.
Skewers come in ones or in bundles of five. The bundle is cheaper by a ryo.
Tea's on the side, if you want something to wash it down.
One skewer of {item}! Careful, the syrup drips.
{pay}. Eat them top to bottom, that's the proper way.
Here you go. Hold it by the stick, not the dango.
That's {pay}. Come back when you've licked the stick clean.
There! Fresh as the morning.
{item}, grilled just now. {pay}, please.
Bundle of five, wrapped in bamboo leaf. Share them, or don't.
That's a bit more than you've got. One skewer instead of five?
Not quite there! Count your ryo again, I'll wait.
Short by a little. Tell you what, come back tomorrow and I'll remember.
Not enough for the bundle, but plenty for a single.
All out of {item}! The Academy let out early.
Sold out. The rice dough needs the night to rest, so tomorrow it is.
No more sweet bean today. Soy glaze?
Haggle over dango? They're already the cheapest thing on the street!
Buy the bundle and it's a ryo less. That's my one secret.
If you can eat five without getting syrup on your sleeve, the next one's free.
I'll give you the slightly lopsided one for less. Tastes just the same.
Last skewers on the grill! After these I'm off home.
The coals are dying down. Grab one while they're warm.
Closing soon. Anything left goes to my neighbours' children.
Training this afternoon? Have a skewer first. Dango gets your chakra coming back faster for a while.
Try the {special}! I've been making them all week and I still can't stop eating them.
The three-colour skewer. Pink for spring, white for winter, green for summer. No autumn, sadly.
Soy glaze if you want something salty, sweet bean if you want to be happy.
The {item}, with a cup of tea. That's a proper break.
Between drills, a single skewer. It keeps your chakra topped up better than you'd think.
My favourite customer! Here, I grilled one extra while you were walking up.
You know, I can tell your step from across the street now.
Usual skewer? I've got it on the coals already.
You've eaten so many dango this season, I should name one after you.
Fresh fish! Caught at dawn, gutted by noon!
Come and look! Eyes clear, gills red, that's how you tell.
Hello, {player}. What'll it be, river or salted?
Welcome! Ignore the smell. It means it's fresh.
Step up! The ice is melting, so everything's moving fast today.
Early bird! The boats only just came in. You get first pick.
Market Day! The coast cart came in, and there's squid and clams today!
River trout, carp and sweetfish on the ice. Salted mackerel hanging up there.
Eel in the tank. Live, so don't put your fingers in.
Dried fish by the string. They keep for weeks, good for long missions.
Shellfish only when the coast cart comes. Clams today, if you're lucky.
Fish heads and bones for stock, nearly free. Ask, and I'll wrap them.
We're shut on Moonday, so buy for two days if you're cooking tomorrow.
Open at dawn, gone by noon. The fish don't wait and neither do I.
{item}, wrapped in leaves. That's {pay}.
There you go! Cook it today, it's too fresh to waste.
That's {pay}. Grill it with salt and nothing else.
Here! I took the bones out for you.
{pay}, thank you. Keep it cool on the walk home.
One {item}. Lovely and firm, that one.
Sold! Tell your friends the trout are fat this week.
That's too much for you today. A string of dried sardines is cheaper.
Short! Come back just before noon, everything's cheaper then.
Not enough, I'm afraid. Fish heads for soup? Those I'll practically give away.
A little under. Smaller fish, then?
No {item} left. The barbecue house bought half the catch.
Sold out! The boats go out again at dawn.
All gone, sorry. The river's been stingy this week.
Haggle all you like, but the fish is getting warmer while we talk.
Buy two and I'll take a ryo off. Fresh fish has to move.
You bargain like a river trader! Fine, a little off. Just this once.
The price drops every hour toward noon. Patience is the best haggle.
Last of the catch, half price! It won't keep till tomorrow!
Closing up! Everything on the ice has to go.
I'm packing the ice away. Take something home for supper.
Noon already. The stall shuts until tomorrow's boats.
Going on a long mission? Dried fish. Light, salty and it won't spoil.
The {item}. Grilled over charcoal, there's nothing better.
Sweetfish, in summer. Salt and a stick through it, that's all it needs.
The {special}. Came up from the coast this morning.
Fish heads and miso make a soup that'll set you up for a whole day of training.
Got a cat? Take the scraps, free. Your cat will think you're a hero.
Saved you the best trout under the ice. Don't tell the barbecue house.
You know your fish now! I watched you check the gills.
My favourite regular. Here, a little extra eel for nothing.
Back again! You eat more fish than the cats at the shelter.
Welcome! Mind the buckets, they're full to the brim.
Come in, {player}. The lilies opened this morning, everything smells of them.
Hello! Looking for something in particular, or just enjoying the colours?
Step in out of the sun. The flowers like the shade, and so will you.
Welcome. Every bloom in here was cut today, I promise.
Welcome to the Yamanaka shop. We've sold flowers on this street longer than the street's had a name.
Winter flowers are few, but camellias and plum branches are in. Come and see.
Roses by the door, chrysanthemums along the wall, potted plants on the steps.
Bouquets are made to order. Tell me who they're for and I'll pick the colours.
Those pots are for apartments. Small, hardy, forgiving if you forget to water them.
Seeds in the paper packets. Plant them in spring, and be patient.
Every flower means something. Ask, and I'll tell you what you're about to say with it.
One {item}. I'll wrap the stems in damp paper.
{pay}, thank you. Change the water every two days.
Here you are. Cut the stem on a slant at home, they'll last longer.
That's {pay}. Whoever gets these will smile.
Lovely choice. {pay}, and I'll tie a ribbon on.
There. Keep it out of direct sun on the walk home.
A {item}, freshly cut. Someone's lucky today.
That bouquet's a little beyond you. A single stem says just as much.
Short, I'm afraid. How about a small pot instead?
Not quite. Come back after a shift, I always need help watering.
A few ryo shy. A sprig of something cheerful, then?
The {item} are all gone. A wedding party cleared them out this morning.
Sold out. The greenhouse has more, but they won't open for a few days.
None left, sorry. Can I suggest something in a similar colour?
Haggling over flowers? They'll wilt while we argue!
A ryo off if you take the ones that opened a day early.
Buy a pot, and I'll throw in a packet of seeds.
I don't lower prices on gifts. A gift should cost a little.
Bringing the buckets in now. Quick, before the blooms close for the night.
Closing up. Anything left I'll press between pages.
Last flowers of the day, a little cheaper. They'll still be pretty tomorrow.
Visiting the hospital? Not potted plants: a pot means staying put. Cut flowers, always.
A {item} for a friend's birthday. Bright and happy.
A small potted plant for your room. It's amazing what one green thing does.
White chrysanthemums are for remembering. Don't bring them to a party.
The {special}. Only in season for a week or two, so this is your chance.
For an apology, purple hyacinth. It's an old meaning, but people know it.
You've a good eye for flowers now. I'll have you making bouquets soon.
There's a sprig of lavender behind the counter with your name on it.
Back again! Whoever you keep buying for is very lucky.
I saved a few stems from the greenhouse for you. Don't tell anyone.
Your bouquet's ready! I added a little green to make the colours sing.
Here's your {item}, wrapped and tied. Whoever it's for will love it.
The arrangement's done. Carry it upright, like a lantern.
All ready. I picked the freshest stems in the greenhouse for this one.
Welcome! Smell that? Fresh cedar. Every piece here came off a bench in the carpenters' lane.
Come in, mind the screens, they're on display, not for leaning.
Furnishing a place, {player}? You've come to the right door.
Hello there. Sit on anything you like, that's what it's for.
In you come. Shoes off on the tatami samples, please.
A new apartment and nothing in it? Everyone starts with a futon and a lamp. We'll fix the rest later.
Futons to the left, low tables in the middle, screens along the back wall.
That weapon rack is solid oak. Holds a dozen kunai and never wobbles.
Cushions come in six colours. The indigo ones hide tea stains best.
The training dummy is straw over a cedar core. Hit it all you like.
Scroll shelves, lamps, potted plants. A room starts feeling lived in with those three.
The pet bed is new. The Inuzuka kennel keeper tested it with three pups.
Posters are cheap and cheerful. The Hokage Rock one sells best.
One {item}. That's {pay}. It'll outlive both of us.
Sold! Want me to tie it up, or will you carry it as is?
{pay}, thank you. Press F at home and set it where the light's best.
There, it's yours. If the joints ever squeak, bring it back and we'll oil them.
A fine pick. {pay}, and I'll throw in a pair of felt pads for the feet.
That's {pay}. Take it slow on the stairs.
Good choice, that {item}. My uncle cut that grain himself.
That piece is out of reach today. The cushions are kinder on a purse.
Not enough for that one, I'm afraid. A few more missions and it's yours.
You're short. I can hold it a day or two if you're close.
Save up for it. Good furniture is worth the wait, cheap furniture is worth nothing.
Last {item} went this morning. The lane will have another off the bench by next week.
Out of those, sorry. Carpenters only have so many hands.
Sold the display one, even. Try the one in the other wood?
I'll take it back at half what you paid. That's the rule, same for everyone.
Half price for anything from this shop, as long as it's whole. Bring it in.
Selling the {item}? Half the price, and it goes back on the floor for someone else.
Changing your room around? I buy back at half. No shame in it.
I buy only what came from here. Bandit junk goes to the pawn shop down the street.
Haggle with me? I'd be haggling with the carpenter who made it, and that carpenter is my aunt.
I can't lower the price of the wood, but I can round down the last few ryo.
Buy the table and the cushions together and I'll take a little off the cushions.
Every price here pays a carpenter's supper. I'll be fair, but I won't be cheap.
Closing up soon. Decide on that lamp before I blow mine out.
I'm sweeping the shavings out in a minute. Last chance tonight.
We shut at dusk. The furniture will still be here tomorrow, I promise.
Nearly closing time. I can hold anything you've got your eye on.
Start with the {item}. It makes the room feel like yours straight away.
A lamp and a potted plant. Cheap, and you'll stop feeling like you live in a box.
A weapon rack keeps your kunai off the floor. Your feet will thank you at night.
If you have a pet, the pet bed. It'll sleep there instead of on your face.
The training dummy, if you've the space. Saves walking to the training grounds every evening.
A scroll shelf. Every shinobi I know ends up with more scrolls than floor.
How's the room looking? I like to picture where my pieces end up.
You again! Your apartment must be the best furnished on the block by now.
I set aside an offcut of cedar for you. Make a little shelf of it, if you like.
My regulars get first look at the new pieces. Come round the back.
Your {item} is finished! The lane sent it over this morning, still smelling of cedar.
The piece you ordered is in. Come and run your hand along that finish.
All done and waiting by the door. Need help carrying it?
Your order's ready. I oiled the joints myself before it left the bench.
Morning greens, evening greens, all day greens! Come and look.
Welcome in. Watch the step, the potato sacks have taken over.
Hello, {player}. Basket's by the door if you need one.
Come in out of the street. Everything in here grew within a day's walk of the gate.
Fresh daikon, fresh eggs, fresh gossip. Two of those are for sale.
Market Day! Half the village is in here, so grab what you need before it's gone.
Busy, busy! The farm carts came in at dawn. Squeeze past the onion crates.
Winter stock: roots, pickles and dried persimmons. The greens will be back in spring.
Onigiri on the left, salted plum or kelp. Rice by the scoop on the right.
The cabbages are heavy this week. Pick one up, you'll see.
Those eggs came from the farm past the east fields. Still warm when I bought them.
Pickles are in the barrels at the back. Lift the lid and let it breathe first.
Mushrooms from the forest edge, picked by people who know which ones are which.
Take your time. I'll be weighing beans if you need me.
{item}, wrapped. That's {pay}.
Here you go. Keep the onigiri out of the sun and they'll last till supper.
{pay}, thank you kindly. Next!
Lovely choice. I'd have taken that one home myself.
One {item}. I put it in paper so it doesn't bruise.
That comes to {pay}. Mind the bag, it's a little damp from the greens.
Sold! Come back when you run out.
Thank you. Tell your neighbours the turnips are sweet this week.
That's more than you've got on you. Want me to set it aside till evening?
Not enough, I'm afraid. A rice ball is cheaper and it'll fill you up.
A few ryo short. I'm hiring for a shift tomorrow, if you're looking for work.
You're just under. Put something back and we'll make it fit.
Gone, every last one of the {item}. The farm cart comes again in two days.
Sold out of onigiri. The Academy lunch crowd got here first.
No eggs left today. The hens are on strike, the farmer says.
A ryo off if you take the bruised ones. They taste the same.
You've got a merchant's tongue! Fine, I'll throw in a carrot. One carrot.
Haggling over turnips? My grandmother would have liked you.
Buy three and I'll knock a little off. That's my only deal, and it's a good one.
Closing soon! The last of the greens are half price, they won't last the night.
I'm bringing the crates in. Anything you want, grab it now.
Evening already. Whatever onigiri's left goes home with me otherwise.
Shutters in a minute. Quick, before I count the till.
Cooking at home? Rice, an egg and some greens in the pot makes a meal that sees you through the afternoon.
Take the {item}. It's at its best right now, and next week it won't be.
Salted plum onigiri for a long walk. They keep, and the salt keeps you going.
Got a cooking pot? Buy a little of everything. Your own cooking is cheaper than eating out.
If you're tired from a late night, a proper meal takes the drag out of your legs for a while.
The {special}. I wouldn't put it at the front if I didn't eat it myself.
Saved you the good cabbage. Don't tell the lady from the tea house.
My best customer! I can tell by the empty basket you've come to fill it.
I put a little bag of dried persimmon aside. It's yours, no charge.
You know where everything is now. I'll stop pointing.
Back again? You eat better than half the Jonin in this village.
Come in, but keep clear of the quench tank. It bites.
Hot in here, isn't it? You get used to it after twenty years.
Welcome to the metalworks. Speak up, my ears went somewhere around my tenth year at the hammer.
Hello, {player}. Steel, chain or powder? I've got all three today.
Welcome to the Hagane works. Our family has poured steel for the Leaf since the wall was wood.
Steel bars on the rack, sold by the bar. Good for kunai, better for a tanto.
Chain by the length. Light links for a weighted cord, heavy ones for a gate.
Powders in the bins: black for bombs, grey for flux. Labelled, so read the labels.
